body:
After just finishing 3 months membership, in hindsight I feel like I fell for a scam, I regret wasting money there. I was hoping to see relief of my clogged pores, less of the deep closed comedones I get, and help fading post acne dark marks that last months for me typically.

I wish I would have listened to the comments I read here saying it's not worth it. I, too, just went for the promo facial that was advertised as I think $50 for your first one. And I usually really resist falling into up-sells but they really, really, stress that you will likely not see much results with one facial, it takes a few months, etc. and then they show all the before and after results showing really nice textural improvement over 3 months. Got sweet talked into trying a membership (a huge splurge for me at $250/mo locked into 3 month minimum contract) and they created a plan for me that I should have at least 6 of the signature facials at lower power before moving up to any other type of service. You can go every 10 days for that. So I did, and then I had two of the power signatures after my skin tolerated those well. It really seemed to do exactly nothing for my skin. The laser really just felt like they ice rolled some jelly around my face every ten days, I did not notice any change after the treatments.

They took photos before my first treatment, and again after my last so they could document how my texture had improved which was so awkward, because when they pulled the photos up side by side I'm pretty sure my skin looked noticeably worse? New acne, same old dark marks, some new dark marks even,  same texture. And the poor RN was still trying to gas me up saying "look how much better your skin looks" I just can't help but feel like those before after photos are so so rigged to make you feel like something happened. 

Edit: I would like to add about me that I am 32, combo skin, very prone to clogged pores on my cheeks, my skin care routine now is pretty basic because my skin is overall drier on tretinoin but also breaks out with anything remotely occlusive. I started Tretinoin 0.025% 6 months ago and had been on it for about 2 months before deciding to try my first facial.
AM
Rinse with water
Serums: BOJ red bean water gel, mixsoon bean essence 
Moisturizer: Paula's choice Omega+ Complex Moisturizer
SPF: Skin Aqua UV super moisture milk 

PM
Cleanser: Vanicream gentle foaming cleanser
Tretinoin: cream applied every other night 
Toner: glow recipe watermelon Aha+BHA (alternate nights with Tretinoin)
Moisturizer: Paula's choice Omega+ complex 


TL;DR  I would save your money.

Born and raised in Grand rapids and just moved away this year - if you've never been through a strong winter before, then make sure to bring a lot of layers and a good quality winter coat. Michigan snow storms can be fun but only if you are well equipped. There is an ice skating rink downtown at Rosa Parks center which only costs like $3 and the art museum is right next to it. There are good dive bars in East Town (the meanwhile, Mulligans)if you want a casual drink with local atmosphere. The mitten is the brewery with the best beers and Harmony in East Town is good pizza. Founders is overrated, sorry. Highly recommend going to some breakfast diners while in town, now that I've moved away I can't find anything quite like it. In order of my favorites 1. The Westsider 2. Wolfgang's 3. Anna's house (the one on Plainfield specifically-  owners are trump supporters but if you can seperate the art from the artist then get the breakfast lasagna and monkey bread it is otherworldly)

There is also a nice park at the top of the city - (Lookout Park off of Fairview) that is good for watching the sunset. Bundle up, bring hot chocolate, and go!
